newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian banks may need provisions for Euro cost.
newsitem.headline: Belgian banks may need provisions for Euro cost.

text.p: Belgian banks may have to start provisioning the exceptional costs linked to the switch to the European single currency, the Euro, in 1999, Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Wednesday.

"Considering the size of the exceptional costs the banking sector will incur, I have asked the Ministry's Secretary General to investigate to what extent certain costs linked to the Euro could not already be provisioned in financial institutions' balance sheets," Maystadt said in a speech at the Belgian Banking Association's annual general meeting.
But he added that only exceptional costs could be provisioned, and not the loss of income from foreign exchange trading that is to be expected when the single currency comes into being.
Late last month the banking association said it wanted the Belgian state to compensate part of the estimated 35 billion franc cost of switching to the Euro.
The association said that converting computer systems to the Euro will cost 15 billion francs, lost income from currency trade 15 billon and the conversion of cash money five billion.
